english_verification.review_scope: Read current L95 history and representative English flavour/formation text, and related fixed-revision country-list/Anzara chunks. The inherited idea descriptions use native English originals. This is English terminology/source review, not exhaustive mission verification.
unresolved: No dedicated Rayaz country-history page was read; related Wiki material does not prove current L95 mechanisms.
Anzara Wiki gives both 1453 and 1454 for its ending; the source discrepancy is retained.
Current native flavour uses Katyradz for the brother; the Chinese rendition is not back-transliterated as a new English name.
Inherited effect-display units remain qualified and Chinese data unchanged.

rationale.campaign_length: 16 direct L95 missions; S81's shared continuation is counted separately.
rationale.colonization: The main activity is on land in Taneyas, not overseas colonisation.
rationale.complexity: Clerical privileges, tribal alliances and formation requirements are intertwined.
rationale.dark_story: Prophetic politics carries risks of oppression, but horror is not the main narrative theme.
rationale.difficulty: Establish the institutional foundations before expanding; no hands-on difficulty assessment was conducted.
rationale.diplomacy: Relations with the Naga, the brother's country and tribal vassals are crucial.
rationale.early_pressure: Strong neighbours and rivalry between brothers demand early consolidation.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Naga prophecy and religious privileges matter, but there is no purely spellcasting gameplay loop.
rationale.narrative_density: Chosen legitimacy, sibling rivalry and a clear connection to the Final Empire give the story continuity.
rationale.tall_play: River cities and government reform matter, but the campaign leans towards expansion.
rationale.trade_economy: River transport, harbours and trade are among the unique storyline's main themes.
rationale.warfare: Integrating the frontier and competitors requires military action.

identity.appearance: An Araskayy lizardfolk Riverclaw tribe in 1444, ruled by Sykar, following the Naga-approved forerunner's route.
identity.formation_scope: Meeting the East Sarhal conditions allows formation of Khatalashya (S81); L95 and L96 are parallel starting countries.
successors: S81 (shared with L96 and other predecessors)

description.text:
For denouncing the decadent Anzaran emperors in 1400, Zerati nagas were expelled from the country for treason. These refugees dispersed among the local tribes, joining up with their naga structure to plot revenge. Their first step was to look for a candidate capable of enforcing their ambitions. Their search stopped in the house of a Riverclaw chieftain, who brought them in to educate his firstborn.
He was just a two year old, sitting and writing today's adventures in his journal. This obviously surprised the nagas, as this was definitely not a normal age to learn how to read and write. But it was a good age to groom their chosen one. The son's name was Sykar. And he was going to be the one to fulfill the naga's ambitions.

description.text: The Twin Academy is a university founded at the entrance of Lasadzanach. There, the minds of the future are educated in two great buildings, connected by a monumental bridge spanning across the Khazynas river. Each side hosts a number of disciplines, the west side teaching the ways of the Sovereign and the east teaching the principles of the Erudite. It’s a place where every layer of lizardfolk society meets, from the poorest to chieftains and emperors - all you have to do is to prove yourself capable enough in the entry exams to become a student of this prestigious establishment.

description.text: One of the first things that Sykar changed when he became the chieftain was to reform the army from a squabble of tribesmen into an organised force. A proper chain of command, standardised formations, a collective fund to supply the army with bronze weapons. These seemingly common ideas were not familiar to the Rayaz before and these improvements were one of the key reasons why the armies of the Naga coalition were able to hold up against professional, battle-hardened armies of Anzara.

description.text: Rayaz was the centerpoint of a vulnerable coalition, split between the Riverclaw brothers, who held together their disparate tribal allies through the unifying efforts of the influential Nagas. These tribes with time became impatient and discouraged by the past war against Zerat, which left them on the verge of breaking ties, but one thing stayed their swords. A prophecy of old, depicted three brothers who would lead the lizardfolk into the 333rd empire. The Nagas preached that the Riverclaws were these prophesied leaders and thus the many tribal allies held onto the glorious vision of helping the Unifier in his attempts to form the Final Empire, foretold to be the final one by the Anzalkatsa teachings.

description.text: Here in the jungles of Taneyas, the roads are rare, unmaintained and obsolete, while the rivers are the lifeblood of trade. Confluences are even more important, serving as a natural joining point for traders. On one of these confluences lies the settlement of Razayas, where the most common trade routes between Zerat and Karassk meet. No matter if you're Anzaran or Karassian, Khugran or Asartan or even human, Rayazas merchants can reach you from there and help you reach new markets faster than the sun sets over the treeline.

description.text: The landscape of the lizardfolk jungles is harsh and unforgiving. You never know what you can step on and your field of view is narrow apart from river crossings. This is a perfect environment for guerilla warfare and it is why the Arraskay tribesmen were able to retain their autonomy from so many empires. A stumble into a toxic flower, a road leading to a wild animal's lair, an ambush on the bridge. Those are only a fraction of many ways you can abuse the element of surprise and anyone who dares enter without our permission will suffer from plenty of them.

description.text: As much as Sykar the Great's reign laid grounds for a massive polity to emerge, so must the effort of his son Sykar the Lawgiver be preached, as he is the one who built a structure to preserve the state from near-fragmentation at the hand of squabbling tribes and Anzaran loyalists. He, unlike his father, integrated himself fully into the naga structures, brought the most influential scholars from across the cities and along with the High Priest Ikhaty codified the law to correct it in line with the morals of the Sculptors of Fate, making it so every lizard lives according to Anzalkatsa teachings.

player_overview.avoid_if: You want to remain in a long unique predecessor tree or dislike religious authority and sibling rivalry.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Secure Naga support and the tribal alliance, develop the river frontier and harbours, then reform the government and work towards Khatalashya.
player_overview.overview: Rayaz is a lizardfolk tribal state in 1444. Its ruler Sykar has Naga support, but must integrate tribes, protect the human frontier, manage waterways and contain rivalry with his brother's Asarta. The compact unique mission tree focuses on preparing for Khatalashya; forming the empire opens the larger shared continuation. If you want a prophesied chosen leader to take a tribe towards empire, this route is more direct than the brother's struggle against fate.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy prophetic legitimacy, lizardfolk tribal integration, river management and a relatively quick entry into an imperial campaign.
signature_features: Naga-approved Sykar and his unchosen brother form a political contrast.
Clerical support, tribal alliances, river trade and a frontier fleet jointly sustain expansion.
16 distinct predecessor missions lead compactly towards a shared Final Empire formable.
player_overview.tagline: Lead the Naga's chosen Riverclaw chief, bringing scattered lizardfolk tribes and the river frontier together as the foundation of the Final Empire.

reasons: A distinctive Naga-chosen perspective and sibling conflict
Compact goals for waterways, defences and tribal integration
A straightforward connection to Khatalashya's shared continuation
warnings: L95's independent mission tree is relatively short.
Clerical and frontier pressures must be managed before formation.

positive_indicators: Integrating scattered tribes into a more stable political order
values.rationale: Frontier protection, river trade and tribal integration provide public benefits. Clerical privileges and competition over prophecy concentrate power and pose risks to local autonomy. Expansion and monarchical reform do not themselves incur a deduction.
red_flags: Power struggles with the brother and local tribes may restrict autonomy.
